preparedDraftChanges.details: All new private helper EXECUTEs explicitly revoked from PUBLIC/anon/authenticated after function creation. Only the already guarded public wrappers and private entrypoints needed by those INVOKER wrappers are granted. Personnel private schema USAGE restored; no table data grant is added.

Current actor, current employee existence and root lock precede request lookup. An exact existing owned request returns its receipt before new-source and stale-CAS checks; altered requests fail. No second event is appended.

Exact command/payload fields; canonical UUIDs; required typed source snapshots and kinds; active person snapshots; string decimal amount/quantity constraints; actual calendar dates/instants; personnel enum/time/date/coverage constraints and required access originals. Cases do not constitute exhaustive fuzzing of all13/15event kinds.

Matches existing domain qualification/task link, planned staffing acknowledgement/own actor, completed prior absence and one-time correction constraints. Source and people snapshots are compared against current prepared loaders. Qualification/delegation, return and correction paths are executed through actual public writers.

Prepared tenant-wide DEFINER source APIs additionally require the existing care_security.company_actor rights, preserving its unrestricted-company-scope ceiling. Synthetic helper bindings prove deny propagation, not the real production helper implementation. Individually scoped record support is not introduced.

Personnel history, context, commit and confirm format actual UTC timestamps before appending Z. Public context containing the complete synthetic ledger reaches the real app decoder even with a Europe/Berlin database session.

appContractFix.reproduction: The actual prepared public SQL commit emits JSONB with reordered object keys. decodeClientFinancingReceipt previously compared JSON.stringify strings and rejected a valid persisted receipt. One actual SQL→decoder test failed before the fix.
changes: Key-order-insensitive existing sameWoundJson for receipt and source-selection comparison, guarded by strict wire-JSON validation.
Finite numbers, strings, member presence and array order remain meaningful; undefined/NaN/sparse arrays/getters/symbols/cycles reject.
Receipt event binds actor/tenant/client/request/event/previousHead/positive integer sequence and recorded microsecond timestamp to the original command.
appContractFix.validation: Actual SQL JSONB receipt passes the real app decoder; changed amount/body, numeric coercion, actor/client/tenant/head/time/version and non-JSON command values fail. Native generation is owned by root.

remainingReleaseBlockers.details: Fresh name catalog still lacks Personnel user_roles, employee_training_records, employee_assignment_eligibility, employee_time_entries, employee_portal_access, employee_hr_documents and Finance client_service_records. Tables were supplied only synthetically in tests; no substitute is chosen by name similarity. Column/types/relations still need exact production mapping.

Current app repositories and old actors assume actor ID equals Auth UID/profile ID. The actual current profile/auth mapping and private auth.sessions column/privilege contract are not established by name-only catalogs. Personnel actor still needs full session freshness/locking reconciliation; extra status/permission/company ceilings are not a complete authentication review.

Tenant-wide new readers now fail closed for limited-company actors via existing company_actor ceiling. Current limited record-specific semantics are unimplemented; broadening to company_record_access needs concrete original record organization mapping and readback tests.

PGlite suite is single connection and uses synthetic prerequisites/helpers. Personnel current source/person selections are not a two-session source-lock/permission-revocation proof. Finance existing table share locks and role locks need actual deadlock/concurrency/performance review. Existing private schema contents/owners/default ACLs/exposed schemas and definition/grant drift require a fresh reviewed gate.

Both packages append evidence ledger records. They do not perform native HR payroll, access-provider revocation, source financing/billing or service-proof original writes. Labels and acceptance must keep those outcomes separate.

No migration or SQL application has been attempted. The older four-packet remains blocked and must not be retried or bypassed. Only a newly compatible, concrete, separately reviewed package can be proposed to the user.
